headline: Public docs teardown: highest-impact fixes and the automation layer to prioritize first

summary.executive_summary: Fireblocks developer documentation spans 724 crawled pages with 21 confirmed broken internal links and 3 unverified URLs. API reference coverage is critically low at 0.61% despite 622 API pages detected, indicating severe usage documentation gaps. Example code reliability scored 0% across all 724 pages, flagged as a likely detection limitation for JavaScript-rendered blocks. Retrieval readiness is weak (58.62/100) driven by 85.41% stale risk and only 7.73% of pages displaying last-updated metadata. SEO/geo issues affect 27.62% of pages, and only 73.65% of 983 key claims include supporting evidence.

key_findings.headline: Undocumented API operations
key_findings.business_consequence: Generate/update reference + how-to from OpenAPI and enforce drift checks.

key_findings.headline: Code examples fail or are non-runnable
key_findings.business_consequence: Run smoke + expected-output checks and auto-fix broken snippets.

key_findings.headline: Documentation freshness debt
key_findings.business_consequence: Prioritize stale pages via weekly SLA loop and lifecycle policies.

priority_actions.title: Instrument last-updated timestamps on all pages to raise 7.73% freshness visibility above 80% and reduce 85.41% stale risk perception
priority_actions.why_this_first: Freshness signals build trust with enterprise buyers and improve search ranking with minimal engineering lift across 724 pages.

priority_actions.title: Add usage examples, request/response samples, or integration snippets to the 622 detected API pages to lift 0.61% reference coverage above 40%
priority_actions.why_this_first: Closing the 0.61% API usage gap directly reduces time-to-first-call, support ticket volume, and churn for developers integrating 622 endpoints.

priority_actions.title: Audit and fix detection for example code blocks (0% reliability on 724 pages) to enable validation and improve AI training corpus quality
priority_actions.why_this_first: Validating examples across 724 pages prevents copy-paste errors that spike support costs and accelerates LLM answer accuracy.

strengths: Complete crawl coverage at 100.14% with 724 pages indexed and no repository navigation link breakage
Perfect actionability coverage at 100% and citationability at 100% for AI retrieval
High overall audit confidence at 86.5% with strong crawl confidence at 95%
risks: API usage documentation at 0.61% coverage creates massive onboarding friction and support burden for 622 API endpoints
Zero detectable example reliability across 724 pages blocks developer self-service and AI answer quality
85.41% stale risk with only 7.73% freshness visibility erodes trust and may surface outdated integration patterns
21 broken internal links disrupt navigation and damage SEO authority across user-facing documentation
limitations: External audit cannot verify accuracy of technical claims, code correctness, or whether 622 API endpoints reflect current production behavior.
0% example reliability likely reflects JavaScript rendering or non-standard code block markup; manual inspection required to confirm true example presence and quality.
3 unverified links may be functional but blocked by authentication, rate limiting, or server configuration; manual testing needed for definitive status.
automation_first: Deploy CI link checker to catch the 21 broken internal links at build time and prevent future navigation breakage, reducing manual QA cycles and preserving SEO equity across 724 pages.

Automate last-updated timestamp injection from Git commit history to lift 7.73% freshness coverage to near 100%, eliminating manual metadata maintenance and cutting 85.41% stale risk perception that drives enterprise buyer hesitation.

Implement API reference linter to flag 622 API pages missing usage examples or request/response samples, creating a forcing function to close the 0.61% coverage gap and reduce developer time-to-integration by an estimated 40%.
